page: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor configured with 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores. The system features a shared CPU allocation running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 320 GB local NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is included. The processor architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the cpx42 demonstrates strong single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both rank in the top 25% of tested instances. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing also show strong performance. Multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests, such as uncached large block reads at 185.88 GB/sec and writes at 51.94 GB/sec, align with mid-tier performance profiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the cpx42 offers a high density of virtual CPU cores and local NVMe storage relative to its resource class, though the shared CPU allocation represents a potential performance tradeoff under sustained multi-core workloads. This resource configuration is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, text processing, software compilation, and light database operations.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 8 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs, 16.0 GB of system memory, and 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating at 2.0 GHz, the processor supports advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 and SHA_NI. Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the cpx42 provides a cost-effective option for workloads that require high core counts and fast local storage but do not demand sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suitable for web serving, text processing, and software compilation.
